dedupe_keys.name: us orphaned oil well aerial imagery and segmentation masks

description: Los Alamos National Laboratory publishes approximately 120,000 aerial-image tiles for locating orphaned oil wells. The Figshare collection separates positive and negative image archives, corresponding segmentation masks and metadata tables. Tiles contain 512 by 512 pixels and derive from US aerial imagery. All six deposits are publicly available and free under CC0. This 2024 release can calibrate asset-detection methods used to assemble well inventories for remediation and environmental-risk simulations, with spatial preparation in platform-qgis. A caveat is that a balanced training collection does not represent the real frequency of abandoned wells. Vegetation and other surface features can obscure wells or produce misleading visual cues. Negative examples should not be interpreted as independently surveyed absence. No imagery, masks or metadata rows were downloaded.
